::: {#thm-deviance-drop}

#### The drop in deviance is the likelihood ratio statistic

Let $D_0$ be the [null deviance](#def-null-deviance) and $D$ the [deviance](#def-deviance) of a logistic regression with $q$ predictors besides the intercept.
Then the [likelihood ratio statistic](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-lrt-stat) of $H_0$: all $q$ slopes are zero is

$$
\lrstat = D_0 - D,
$$

and for a large sample it has approximately a $\chi^2_q$ distribution under $H_0$.

:::

::: proof
Under $H_0$ the model is the intercept-only model, so $\llikf{\hparam_0} = -D_0 / 2$.
The unrestricted maximum is $\llikf{\hvcoef} = -D / 2$.
Substituting both into the [likelihood ratio statistic](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-lrt-stat) gives $\lrstat = 2 \paren{-D/2 + D_0/2} = D_0 - D$.
The limiting distribution follows from [Wilks' theorem](intro-MLEs.qmd#thm-wilks) with $q$ constraints.
:::
